sentences.text: Garrigatitan was a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur that lived during the late Cretaceous Period in France.
This genus contains only one known species, Garrigatitan meridionalis.
The name Garrigatitan combines the Occitan word for a dry thicket and the Greek word for a giant.
A tentatively referred adult specimen is estimated to have been 12 to 16 meters long.
The holotype fossil is a sacrum belonging to an immature individual of Garrigatitan.
Excavations to find Garrigatitan fossils took place at Velaux-La Bastide Neuve between 2009 and 2012.
Garrigatitan meridionalis was named and described in 2021 by a team led by Verónica Díez Díaz.
The holotype specimen of Garrigatitan dates to the late Campanian stage of the Cretaceous.
Initial phylogenetic analysis placed Garrigatitan within the titanosaur subfamily Lirainosaurinae.
A 2024 analysis recovered Garrigatitan as a non-lirainosaurine titanosaur within the clade Lognkosauria, related to genera like Notocolossus and Patagotitan.
Garrigatitan is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Garrigatitan lived approximately 74 to 70 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the late Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
The time range for Garrigatitan is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
